whatItDoes: A browser study that adds a creep-governed HMPE replacement line to a line-by-line port of Skyhook's finance/skyhook_finance.py and solves it backwards for the required life. It never prints a predicted life. For the conservative 2.5 km/s case (all-HMPE, launch $2,500/kg only, fiber unpriced, rolling 1/L-per-year convention), payback stays at Y17 only if the HMPE lasts at least 28.46 years (14.25 for Y18). Below 19.04 years replacement costs more than the $80M fixed-ops line, and below 1.90 years the case never pays back. The anchored datum is SK78 at about 8 yr at 20% load, and the taper-weighted founding-doc HMPE share of 99.63% gives 28.4 years. The page refuses to compute anything until an HMPE share is chosen (it shows only "28.5 years × the share"). It refuses a base case that never pays back (3.5 km/s), the 15-year window where the base case already misses it, and bad inputs. It also offers a lumpy convention (13.0 years for Y17), a DM20 tick (8 × 50 = 400 yr, tick only) and a [Speculative] ST-002 creep-rate-ratio reading (14.1×).
testsPin:
model.test.mjs has 25 tests and pins these external numbers:
- The published conservative triple $8,741M / Y17 / −$3,883M, parsed from the DECISION_LOG snapshot (:47, :57), plus the Baseline and Optimistic triples of item 6.
- All five EQ-6 mass ratios and fiber masses in rev_a.json's mass_ratio block (40.32/64.30/121.83/295.27/3085.95; 201.6/321.5/609.1/1476.3/15429.8 t).
- Skyhook's own finance module run live through crosscheck.py (python3 -B, bytecode off): every flow, payback, NPV and closed-form L* for 9 tier × column cases and 10 replacement runs each must match to 1e-12, and erf must match math.erf to 1e-14.
- erf at 0.5, 1 and 2 against tabulated values (A&S Table 7.1, quoted from memory and confirmed by math.erf).
- The proposal's hand check, 609.1304 t × $2,500 / 8 = $190.35M/yr.
- A hand-worked exact-zero cash flow that pins the strict "> 0" payback rule (skyhook_finance.py:25).
- Simpson integration of the EQ-6 taper profile, for both the 99.63% mass share and the identity that the profile integral is EQ-6.
- Every quoted line checked byte-for-byte against its snapshot line, and the README's numbers checked against the code.

ui-check.mjs (53 checks, 390 px dark by touch and 1280 px light by keyboard) compares every number on the page with model.js. It checks the refusals, the DM20 toggle leaving the tested life alone, no overflow, no console errors and no network requests.

Sabotage, each mutation applied alone and counted as failing node tests / failing ui-check checks:
- Replacement sign flipped: 7/0.
- Replacement starting in Y4: 6/0.
- Closed form using Y−5: 5/0.
- erf truncated at 1e-6: 3/0.
- Payback on cum ≥ 0: 1/0.
- Ramp step 0.2: 7/0.
- Lumpy event booked a year late: 2/0.
- Zylon counted in both arms: 2/0.
- Load fraction taken from derate: 1/1.
- DM20 factor applied to the SK78 tick: 1/1.
- v_orb from rev_a's 6,988 km radius: 1/0. Only the live cross-check catches this, and it skips without the checkout.
- Unpriced fiber silently priced at $1,000/kg: 9/0.
- Hardware mass factor applied to replacement: 7/0.
- Page: DM20 toggle scaling the tested life: 0/2.
- Page: a life printed before a share is chosen: 0/6.

findingsAboutSourceRepo:
Skyhook at 34935cb:
1. finance/skyhook_finance.py:259 books opex as var*m + fixed_ops_M. DECISION_LOG item 10 outcome (a), "creep-governed tether replacement cadence, costed into ops" (docs/DECISION_LOG.md:74), has no cost line anywhere under finance/, and no file there mentions creep.
2. tools/financial/skyhook_risk_register.xlsx (sheet Risk Register, rows 5–16) has no creep row. docs/research/mp001_market_pricing.md:57 asks to "update the UHMWPE-creep row", which does not exist. docs/program_manifest.md:39 correctly says "add: UHMWPE creep", and docs/DECISION_LOG.md:78 still lists the row update as an open downstream action.
3. params/rev_a.json materials.construction_baseline ("Spectra/UHMWPE core + Zylon outer arm (Hoytether architecture)") does not state the hybrid boundary, and can be read as a whole Zylon arm. docs/project_instructions.md:108 says "outer ~20 km of the lower arm". The HMPE share that every creep cost depends on is not in canon.
4. The only creep life (mp001_market_pricing.md:23, "SK78 ≈ 8 yr at 20% load, 20 °C") is for SK78, but rev_a.json alternative_fibers carries SK99 strength (3.6 GPa), and MP-001:22 puts SK99 15–20% above SK78. The life and strength data are for different grades, and the life's failure criterion (rupture or an elongation limit) is not stated.
5. The judged proposal's third judge note says MP-001 line 46 carries the DM20 ">50×" figure. It is in docs/research/lr001_splice_literature.md:45; DECISION_LOG:74 cites it correctly.

Also noted, but not a defect: the conservative payback rests on $695.49M of cumulative slack at Y17, so any line averaging more than $53.5M a year moves it to Y18.
deviationsFromProposal:
- The proposal's ladder.json does not exist in Skyhook. build_data.py derives it from tools/financial/skyhook_financial_model.xlsx using only the standard library (zipfile + xml.etree), with rows named by skyhook_finance.py's own _LADDER_ROWS. It also derives the cash-flow conventions (ast), R_EARTH_KM from physics/skyhook_physics.py:40, and the founding-doc sentence, each with a sidecar.
- Added a taper-weighted mass reading of the founding-doc boundary (99.63%) next to the proposal's length reading (96.875%), because the Zylon sits at the thin tip.
- Added a lumpy replacement convention as a labelled sensitivity. Its answer (13.0 yr for Y17) is so far from rolling's (28.5) that showing one alone would hide a choice.
- The proposal's boundary test "payback(L*) = 18" was made exclusive, tested at L*(1−1e-9). At L* exactly the cumulative cash flow is zero and round-off decides.
- "28–40% load" became the chosen column's own load, (1−derate)/SF = 28/34/40%.
- Before a share is chosen, the page shows the exact per-share scaling (28.5 yr × share) instead of nothing.
- Added a [Speculative] ST-002 creep-ratio reading and an HMPE-grade mass sensitivity (SK99 at 0.97 g/cm³ gives 122.60×; SK78 strength would make the tether 1.70–2.03× heavier), each with its assumptions stated.
- The DM20 tick is labelled a lower bound ("> 400 yr") that rests on life ∝ 1/creep rate.
- Launch price stays tied to the column; there is no switch for a cheaper replacement-era price, to avoid the DECISION_LOG item 7 mixed-case error. The README states the linear scaling instead (7.2 yr at the speculative $629/kg).
- Kept from the proposal: the never-predict rule, the inspace_fork-style unpriced badge, the fixed-ops crossing, and the closing sentence.
notBuilt:
- No sourced creep life at 28–40% load exists in the checkouts, so the page cannot say whether any real grade meets the requirement. It only frames the gap; the ST-002 reading is labelled [Speculative].
- Swap hardware, installation operations, downtime and lost revenue are not costed. The hardware mass factor is not applied to replacement. Every required life is therefore a floor at the column's launch price.
- The 2.8 and 3.5 km/s rows are the finance model's partial tier model, not those tiers' business cases.
- I did not reproduce Skyhook's breakeven figures ($686/kg, $517/kg, SENSITIVITY_FINDINGS thresholds).
- There is no Python port or pytest test inside Skyhook. crosscheck.py imports Skyhook's finance module read-only, but none of Skyhook's gates (Rule 1 canon, VM verification, pytest suite) have been passed.
- The erf table values are quoted from memory of A&S Table 7.1 and confirmed against Python's math.erf, not against the printed table.
- The v_orb-radius mutation is caught only when the Skyhook checkout and openpyxl are present. Without them the cross-check test skips.
